:question/problem:
The three vectors share an origin, and each grid square has the same side length.

![](images/01/011827ed9170f302628f66a6ccfded83be2e8d966be3977cf3cbf86d8dec5386.png)

Given $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}$, find $\lambda$.
:question/worked-solution:
Draw $2\mathbf{b}$ from the common origin $O$ to a point $P$, then complete the path from $P$ to the endpoint $C$ of $\mathbf{c}$.

![](images/ce/cee2a501a390c40bc1100336ff4a7cda3e7a070dff7dc0470b1762833a7a677a.png)

The vector $\overrightarrow{PC}$ points left, while $\mathbf{a}$ points right. Their lengths are equal, so
$$
\overrightarrow{PC}=-\mathbf{a}.
$$
Adding the two path vectors gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{c}&=\overrightarrow{OP}+\overrightarrow{PC}\\
&=2\mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a}\\
&=-\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}.
\end{aligned}
$$
Because $\mathbf{a}$ and $\mathbf{b}$ are nonparallel, their coefficients are unique. Comparing with $\mathbf{c}=\lambda\mathbf{a}+2\mathbf{b}$ gives $\lambda=-1$. The minus sign records direction; the equal lengths give magnitude $1$.
